newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian leader's health satisfactory after checks.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian leader's health satisfactory after checks.

text.p: Alija Izetbegovic, the chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, went back to work on Wednesday after a five-day stay in hospital for scheduled medical treatment, his aide said.
"He's happy to be back," said Mirza Hajric, a spokesman for Izetbegovic.
Doctors gave the Moslem member of the three-man presidency medical tests nearly a year after he suffered a heart attack.
Doctor Enver Raljevic at Kosevo hospital's heart clinic told Reuters that Izetbegovic was in good health.
"We performed a test on his heart which showed his condition was satisfactory," Raljevic said.
During his hospital stay, the collective presidency met with Haris Silajdzic, the co-chairman of the central cabinet, standing in for Izetbegovic.

The 71-year old Izetbegovic led Bosnia through 43 months of war after it declared independence from Serbian-dominated Yugoslavia. He signed the Dayton peace treaty that ended the conflict in November 1995.
